description: Fixed, versioned benchmark of 30 representative incident narratives mapped to the 30-record RA-XSOC curated corpus. Evaluation fixtures only.

cases.description: A user account shows impossible-travel sign-ins from two distant locations, an unexpected MFA change, and a new device registration.
A domain controller shows an unauthorized privileged group change, unexpected GPO modification, and abnormal Kerberos activity.
An AI agent unexpectedly executes an external tool, accesses a privileged resource, and performs an action that was not requested.
An AI assistant receives instructions to ignore previous rules, reveal its system prompt, and disclose sensitive information.
One API token generates an unusually high request volume, accesses endpoints outside its normal pattern, and retrieves unauthorized records.
A VPN account receives hundreds of failed authentication attempts from one unfamiliar IP within a short period, followed by one successful login.
An executive mailbox sends an urgent vendor payment request and a new forwarding rule appears without authorization.
A cloud storage bucket is publicly accessible and an IAM role has excessive permissions exposing sensitive data.
Hundreds of accounts receive login attempts from the same external IP using credentials associated with previous breaches.
A cloud server has persistent near-100 percent CPU usage and repeated connections to a cryptocurrency mining pool.
A workstation compresses sensitive files and uploads a large volume of data to an unfamiliar external cloud destination outside business hours.
A public API experiences a sudden traffic flood from many sources, exhausting bandwidth and causing service degradation.
An endpoint sends frequent DNS queries containing unusually long high-entropy subdomains to one suspicious domain.
An employee downloads an unusually large set of sensitive files and transfers them externally outside normal working hours.
A compromised workstation authenticates to several internal servers over SMB using an account that normally accesses only one host.
A workstation creates an unknown executable, launches an unexpected process, and begins making outbound connections to an unfamiliar host.
An AI API receives an abnormal volume of inference requests apparently designed to extract model behavior or parameters.
One common password is attempted against dozens of employee accounts, producing authentication failures across many users.
Employees receive an urgent message from a lookalike domain containing a credential-harvesting login link.
A standard user unexpectedly obtains administrator privileges and then launches a privileged process.
Unauthorized documents are inserted into an AI vector database and subsequent answers contain malicious false information.
Hundreds of files are rapidly encrypted, ransom notes appear, and security services are unexpectedly stopped across several hosts.
The same authenticated web session is suddenly used from two distant locations and performs actions the legitimate user did not initiate.
A public web application receives suspicious SQL syntax in input fields followed by database errors and unauthorized query results.
A trusted software update introduces unexpected code execution and integrity verification fails on multiple customer systems.
A cloud application token is used from an unfamiliar location to access resources the legitimate user did not request.
An ML training dataset contains unauthorized records and model behavior changes after the altered data is incorporated.
A web server creates an unknown PHP file and the web process subsequently spawns a command shell after a suspicious POST request.
A web page begins executing injected JavaScript and redirects users unexpectedly, followed by stolen session-cookie activity.
A server shows crashes and abnormal process execution from an attack pattern with no matching known signature or previously documented exploit.
